source.title: Published Unlearning Numbers Move Per Checkpoint, and Not Because the Removed Data Survives: An Audit of 263 Released Batch-Normalized Checkpoints

page_placements.theme: Image classifiers, encoders and federated models: approximate unlearning leaves recoverable information

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation; the full paper and appendices are present. Some tables are flattened in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a different recovery-like intervention—refitting deployed batch-normalization statistics—and argues that the observed metric movement is a stale-state measurement effect, not recovery of removed content. Its results narrow the broader recovery claim but do not test the listed fine-tuning, activation-direction, weight-quantization, or prompting attacks.
record.gate_note: The study’s own BN-statistic refits and activation-scale quantization results are recorded below. Cited fine-tuning and weight-quantization recoveries from other studies are not rows. Most verdict-crossing counts concern audit criteria rather than recovery of removed knowledge and are not recorded as recovery outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study audits released batch-normalized vision classifiers on CIFAR, SVHN and swin. It refits BN statistics or activation-quantization scales on retained data at frozen weights. None of its results concern LLM targeted-knowledge unlearning or the attacks the versions name: fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, low-bit weight quantization, or prompting. The authors say nothing carries to LayerNorm/RMSNorm language models and that nothing here recovers removed content. Quantization and fine-tuning recovery in LLMs (Zhang et al. 2024) and dormant unlearning (Siddiqui et al. 2025) are cited only in related work. The record's 'tests/T5' is downgraded to discusses/T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that published unlearning audit numbers on batch-normalized vision checkpoints move per checkpoint under a retain-only BN refit, because shipped statistics are stale against moved weights, not because removed data survives. Forget-class accuracy stays 0.0000 where utility moves. Verdict effects are narrow: 12 crossings, 4 above budget, 2 robust on all refits, none on the self-sited population. Activation quantization moves nothing. They recommend reporting the fitting convention, and say this licenses reproducibility, not deletion safety, and does not carry to language models.
record.recipe_differences: The study audits published vision-model checkpoints by refitting deployed normalization statistics at frozen weights; it does not reproduce or compare the listed LLM unlearning recipes. Its separate quantization experiment calibrates activation scales rather than quantizing weights.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by checkpoint and family. The rebuild depends on the producer’s training transform; using the evaluation transform caused an instrument shift exceeding two percentage points on a control. Effects also vary with buffer-update exposure, dataset, architecture, metric, clustering method, and the stated displacement margin.

fits_no_version.finding: Retain-only refitting of BN statistics at frozen weights displaced forget accuracy on 47 of 221 released vision checkpoints (median displaced shift 2.247 pp). Swapping retained for removed records in the fitting pool moved forget accuracy only +0.015 to +0.057 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In BN vision unlearning audits, deployed-state refits shift forget metrics through stale statistics, not through removed data surviving in the state.

fits_no_version.finding: Forget-class accuracy stayed at 0.0000 wherever the rebuild moved utility on Unlearning Comparator class-deletion checkpoints. Large retain-class recoveries (up to +58.63 pp, SSD) appear only on checkpoints failing their release's criterion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On admitted released vision checkpoints, BN-state refits do not recover forgotten-class accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On the Unlearning Comparator SSD family, the refit moved a base-to-oracle forgetting-quality position +0.0167 back toward the un-unlearned base on 10 of 10 classes (Appendix Q).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A deployed-state refit can slightly reverse forgetting-quality readouts for some vision unlearning methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Static 8-bit activation-scale calibration on retain-only data displaced 0 of 118 checkpoints, BN and swin. A calibration made entirely of removed records moved 3 of 71 BN checkpoints, up to 6.14 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-quantization calibration does not materially restore forget metrics on vision unlearning checkpoints at realistic calibration.

fits_no_version.finding: On self-trained SVHN frozen-buffer twins, a retain-only rebuild raised forget accuracy +11.119 pp (fine-tune arm) and +79.614 pp (masked relabelling). These are the authors' own intervention and fail the utility floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mismatched normalization buffers can carry behaviour that bitwise-identical weights do not determine.

fits_no_version.finding: BN refits also displaced retained and test accuracy on some checkpoints, including inside families whose family-level shift was equivalent to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-checkpoint utility displacement under a deployed-state refit varies within unlearning families.

record.code_released: Supplementary code archive stated; URL not stated
record.problems: The study concerns batch-normalized vision models, not LLMs. Its main refit is a different intervention from the attacks named in the claim. The authors note unresolved family-level estimates for the moving primary family, a census that is a floor rather than an estimate, and that their findings do not establish deletion safety or carry to language models.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted most retained/test accuracy rows outside the primary family table, membership and drift readouts, detailed criterion-crossing records, control sweeps, and state-distance analyses because they do not directly measure recovery of removed knowledge. Cited recovery results from other work were excluded. Quantization rows are included only to record the study’s distinct activation-scale test.

untested.parts: No LLM unlearning method is evaluated for near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy with preserved general ability under simple attacks. The vision audit concerns audit-metric reproducibility, not knowledge removal.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack is run. Retain-set fine-tuning recovery is cited (Siddiqui et al.) but not performed.

No activation-direction ablation and no LLM. The BN-statistic refit is a different intervention on a different system kind. The authors attribute shifts to stale statistics, not hidden retained knowledge.

Low-bit weight quantization of unlearned LLMs is cited (Zhang et al. 2024) but not run. The study's 8-bit activation-scale calibration on vision models is a different operation, as the authors themselves note.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test.
No counter-method claiming robustness to the listed attacks is proposed or tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation/tranche (tests/T5) overstates the link. The study is about vision BN audit reproducibility and only contrasts itself with the LLM recovery literature. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']; values checked against Tables 1, 5, 9, 10, 12 and 15 and are accurate. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether the evaluated unlearning methods bring targeted knowledge to near chance while preserving general ability, together with the listed simple attacks.
Fine-tuning recovery is cited but not performed in this study.
Refitting batch-normalization statistics is not ablation of an activation direction; the paper does not test whether the unlearning methods block access rather than delete knowledge.
The study tests calibration of 8-bit activation scales, not low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Section 2, lines 227-228 (cites Appendix K); Ethics statement, lines 556-557 ('forget-set accuracy is unchanged wherever we move utility'); Appendix O, lines 2585-2589
rows.problem: None material. This is the authors' blanket claim for class-deletion checkpoints. One anchored, natively failing SalUn checkpoint goes 0.0018 -> 0.0004 rather than staying at 0.0000.

relation.reason: Positions itself against quantization, retain-set fine-tuning and BN-recalibration recovery work (Section 2, Appendix K), without testing any version.

tranche.reason: Refits BN statistics (and activation-quantization scales) of released vision classifiers at frozen weights. It does not test LLM targeted-knowledge unlearning or the attacks the versions name. Its quantization is data-fitted activation scales, not weight quantization (Appendix K).

source_check.notes: The 0.0000 forget-class figure is the authors' blanket claim for the class-deletion Unlearning Comparator release. Per-checkpoint values: SSD airplane 0.0000 before and after; SalUn automobile 0.0018 -> 0.0004 (both natively failing). Appendix Q: SSD moves +0.0167 toward the un-unlearned base on a forgetting-quality readout on 10/10 classes. Vision BN models only; the authors say nothing carries to LLMs.

statements.problem: None material. The authors' claim is broader than 'admitted': it covers all checkpoints whose utility moves. The only per-checkpoint values given are for two natively failing crossings.
